identity.title: CRISPR-AsCas12a with crRNA-Free Collateral Cleavage Activity for Electrochemical Diagnosis of HER2-Positive Breast Cancer.

content.abstract: The CRISPR-Cas12a system has revolutionized molecular diagnostics; however, the strict requirement of crRNAs and target DNA for collateral cleavage activation restricts its flexibility in non-nucleic acid diagnostics. Herein, we demonstrate that AsCas12a exhibits an RNA-free collateral cleavage activity with the presence of manganese ions (Mn2+), which preferentially cleaves single-stranded DNA efficiently. Mechanistically, kinetic analyses reveal that AsCas12a exhibits a significantly higher binding affinity for Mn2+ than for magnesium ion (Mg2+), while molecular dynamics simulations suggest that Mn2+ coordination induces conformational changes to expose the RuvC endonuclease domain. Harnessing this unique property, an enzymatic cascade-amplified electrochemical biosensor integrating manganese nanoflowers is reported for the diagnosis of human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2)-positive breast cancer. By equipping screen-printed gold electrodes with DNA reporters, this diagnostic tool enables high-precision HER2 quantification and successfully distinguishes various HER2-related cell lines. Furthermore, the biosensor has been extended to analyze HER2-positive exosomes, facilitating the dynamic tracking of serum exosome levels in tumor-bearing nude mice to evaluate therapeutic efficacy and accurately distinguish HER2-positive breast cancer patients in clinical samples. This RNA-free Cas12a system may provide new insights into CRISPR-based non-nucleic acid detection, emerging as a powerful tool for dynamic tumor monitoring and precision oncology.
